title: Rara Lake Travel Guide: Routes, Costs and Best Time
meta_description: Rara Lake travel guide: flight, helicopter, jeep and trekking routes compared, best months, permits, lodges, costs from India and a packing list.
summary: Rara Lake, at about 2,990 m in Mugu district, is Nepal's largest lake and one of its least visited highlights. Reach it by a 45-minute flight from Nepalgunj to Talcha, a helicopter, two days by jeep or a 5–6 day trek from Jumla. Go April–June or September–November, and expect basic lodges and cold nights.

sections.heading: Rara Lake at a glance
paras: Rara sits in a forested basin in Karnali Province, far from Nepal's main tourist routes. The lake is about 5.1 km long and 2.7 km wide, with a surface of 10.8 km² and a maximum depth of 167 m. It lies inside Rara National Park, declared in 1976 and covering 106 km², and in 2007 the lake and its wetlands were listed as a Ramsar site. The villages that once stood on the shore were moved out when the park was created, so the shoreline is almost empty.

What makes Rara special is not a single sight but the setting: deep blue water that changes shade through the day, blue pine, spruce and juniper to the waterline, and snow ranges such as Kanjiroba and Saipal on the horizon from the surrounding ridges. It is quiet for most of the year. Domestic tourism has grown fast, with crowds in October and around the Nepali New Year in mid-April, but foreign visitors remain few.

sections.heading: Four ways to reach Rara compared
paras: Every route to Rara starts in Nepalgunj, the hub of western Nepal, reached by an hour's flight from Kathmandu or a 4–5 hour drive from Lucknow via the Rupaidiha border. From there you choose between speed, cost and experience.

The scheduled flight to Talcha is the best balance for most travellers: 45 minutes in a small plane, then a gentle walk. A helicopter is fastest and suits day trips or older relatives, at a much higher price. The jeep road through Surkhet and Jumla is cheap but long and rough. Trekking from Jumla takes most time but gives the richest journey, through meadows, passes and the historic Sinja valley.

sections.heading: Best time to visit Rara Lake
paras: Spring, from April to early June, brings warm days of 15–20 °C, rhododendrons on the ridges and wildflowers in the meadows. Nights still drop close to freezing. Autumn, from late September to November, gives the clearest skies, the deepest blue water and the best mountain views from Murma Top, with cold nights below zero by November.

The monsoon, July and August, turns the hills green but brings rain, cloud and frequent flight cancellations, and landslides close the road. Winter, December to March, is very cold, with snow in the forest and ice on the lake edges in January; flights and the road are often disrupted. Hardy travellers do visit in winter for solitude, but we do not recommend it for first-timers.

sections.heading: Permits, fees and rules
paras: You need a Rara National Park entry permit, paid at the park office or arranged by your agency. Foreign nationals pay more than SAARC nationals, including Indians, and Nepali citizens pay a nominal fee. Trekkers coming from Jumla also need a TIMS card, and current rules require foreign trekkers in most of Nepal to walk with a licensed guide. No restricted area permit is needed for Rara. Fees change, so check current status before you travel.

The park is guarded by the Nepal Army. Fishing and swimming are not allowed, camping is limited to approved sites, and drones need prior permission. Keep to trails around the shore and carry out all rubbish; there is no waste collection beyond what lodges manage themselves.

sections.heading: Where to stay at Rara
paras: There are no resorts at Rara. A few lodges and community homestays operate near the park office on the south-east shore and in Talcha village by the airstrip. Rooms are twin or triple with blankets, shared toilets and occasional hot water from solar heaters. Meals are dal bhat, noodles, potatoes, eggs and tea. Electricity comes from solar panels, so a power bank is useful, and mobile signal is patchy.

In peak weeks domestic tourists fill rooms, and our groups either book well ahead or bring tents and a cook for approved campsites. Whatever the season, bring a warm sleeping bag; even in May the lodges are cold at night. In Nepalgunj before and after, hotels such as Siddhartha Hotel give a comfortable base with air-conditioning and a pool.

sections.heading: Things to do at Rara Lake
paras: The classic activity is the 13 km walk around the lake, mostly level at about 3,000 m and taking 4–5 hours. Go clockwise in the morning for the best light on the north shore. The second is a pre-dawn climb of about two hours to Murma Top, around 3,630 m, for sunrise over the whole lake with Kanjiroba and Saipal behind.

Strong, acclimatised walkers can climb Chuchemara Danda, 4,087 m, on a long day with a local guide. Birders watch for Himalayan monal in the forest and coots, grebes and ducks on the water in winter. The small Thakur Baba temple on the shore is a peaceful stop. Many visitors simply sit by the water and watch its colours change.

sections.heading: What a Rara trip costs
paras: Indicative prices per person, twin sharing, from our current packages: a 5-day Rara tour by flight from Kathmandu starts from about ₹62,000 or US$730, including flights via Nepalgunj, hotels, Rara lodges and meals there, and a guide. An 8-day overland trip from Lucknow combining Bardia and Rara starts from about ₹68,000. The 12-day trek from Jumla starts from about US$1,620. A shared seat on a helicopter day tour starts from about ₹1,15,000.

The main cost drivers are mountain flights and, on the trek, camping crew. Groups of four or more pay less per person. Budget extra for a possible additional night in Nepalgunj if a flight is cancelled.

sections.heading: Packing list for Rara
paras: Mountain flights usually allow 15 kg including hand luggage, so pack light and leave extra bags in Nepalgunj.
list: Sleeping bag rated to about −5 °C, or −10 °C in November
Down or synthetic insulated jacket, fleece, warm hat and gloves
Waterproof jacket and trousers for spring and early autumn showers
Comfortable walking shoes or light boots
Headtorch for the Murma Top sunrise climb
Sunglasses, sunscreen and lip balm for strong high-altitude sun
Power bank, as electricity is solar and limited
Enough Nepali cash for the whole stay; there are no ATMs

faqs.a: Yes, for travellers who value quiet landscapes over facilities. Rara is Nepal's largest lake, set among pine forest with snow peaks on the horizon, and it sees far fewer visitors than Pokhara or Gosaikunda. Lodges are basic and access depends on mountain flights, so it suits flexible, outdoorsy travellers.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Rara Lake?
faqs.a: Five days from Kathmandu by flight, with two nights at the lake, is the practical minimum. Add a day for flight delays if you can. The trek from Jumla takes 12 days door to door. A helicopter day tour from Nepalgunj fits in one morning but gives only 1–1.5 hours at the lake.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to reach Rara Lake?
faqs.a: By road. Buses and shared jeeps run from Nepalgunj via Surkhet to Jumla on the Karnali Highway, and onward jeeps reach the Rara area, taking two days or more. It is cheap but long, rough and uncomfortable, and roads close during the monsoon. Flights are much faster for a modest extra cost.

faqs.q: Is Rara Lake safe for families?
faqs.a: Yes, for families with children around eight and older who can manage a short walk from Talcha and simple lodges. The lake circuit is level and safe. Watch children near the water, which is deep and cold, and keep them warm at night. The altitude of about 2,990 m is usually fine for healthy children.

faqs.q: Can I see snow at Rara Lake?
faqs.a: From December to March the forest and surrounding ridges are usually under snow, and the lake edges freeze in January. In spring and autumn snow is visible only on distant peaks such as Kanjiroba and Saipal from Murma Top. Winter travel is possible but flights and roads are often disrupted.

Rara Lake is at about 2,990 m. Talcha airstrip is around 2,700 m, Murma Top about 3,630 m and Chuchemara Danda 4,087 m. Most healthy visitors cope well, but some feel breathless or sleep poorly on the first night after flying up from Nepalgunj at 150 m.

faqs.q: Are there ATMs or shops at Rara?
faqs.a: There are no ATMs at Rara or Talcha, and shops sell only basics such as biscuits, noodles and soft drinks. Carry all the Nepali cash you need from Nepalgunj or Kathmandu. Lodges usually accept cash only. Bring any medicines, snacks and toiletries you rely on.

Yes. Rara is open to all nationalities with a national park entry permit. No restricted area permit is required. Trekkers need a TIMS card and, under current rules, a licensed guide. Fees for foreign nationals are higher than for SAARC nationals; check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Rara Lake better than Phewa Lake in Pokhara?
faqs.a: They are very different. Phewa is a lowland lake beside a busy city, with hotels, boating and cafés. Rara is a high, remote lake inside a national park, with basic lodges and almost no development. Choose Pokhara for comfort and easy access, Rara for solitude and a sense of adventure.
